newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end last 1996/97 session weak.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end last 1996/97 session weak.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures finished the last trading session of the 1996/97 financial year weakly on Monday with disappointment over the Japanese government's plans to boost land liquidity weighing on the market.
Dealers said details of the plans in the business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun caused some selling in early trade and June Nikkei futures were dragged sharply lower by stop-loss sales in the afternoon.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 June contract lost 330 points to end at 17,875 on low volume of 8,080 lots.
"When it tested 18,000 and went below, I guess there was some panic selling. And some stops must have gone off for the move to be so rapid," said a dealer with a Japanese institution.

The government announced a series of measures to improve land liquidity after the market closed, including easing rules to allow the securitisation of collateralised real estate and the use of 380 billion yen of tax money to buy land.
"The market was disappointed at the size of the help the government was giving. It's just like throwing pennies into a black hole," said a trader with a European futures house.
Dealers said market participation was likely to be limited ahead of the Bank of Japan's quarterly business sentiment survey, or tankan, on Wednesday.
The June Nikkei is expected to remain supported around 17,770-17,800, with resistance seen persisting above 18,300.
The April MSCI Taiwan index contract ended at 319.3 against its opening 336.0 on volume of 1,131 lots.
